findings.title: Liability is not capped
findings.excerpt: The Receiving Party shall indemnify the Disclosing Party against any and all losses, without limitation.
findings.explanation: An uncapped indemnity exposes the client to damages far beyond the value of the relationship. Propose a cap, for example the fees paid in the previous 12 months, and exclude indirect damages.

findings.title: Confidentiality never expires
findings.excerpt: The obligations under this Agreement shall survive indefinitely.
findings.explanation: Perpetual obligations are hard to comply with and to enforce. A term of 3 to 5 years after disclosure is common, with longer protection only for trade secrets.

findings.title: No governing law or jurisdiction
findings.explanation: The agreement does not say which law applies or which court decides disputes. Add both, so that a dispute does not start with a dispute about where to litigate.

findings.title: Tenant pays for structural repairs
findings.excerpt: All maintenance and repair works, including those relating to the structure of the building, shall be borne by the Tenant.
findings.explanation: Structural and extraordinary repairs are normally the landlord's responsibility. Shifting them to the tenant can cost more than the rent itself; limit the tenant's duty to ordinary maintenance.

findings.title: Rent indexed at 100% of inflation
findings.excerpt: The rent shall be updated every year by 100% of the change in the consumer price index.
findings.explanation: For this type of lease, indexation above 75% of the ISTAT index may not be allowed. Verify it and negotiate the percentage down.

findings.title: Rent indexed at 100% of inflation
findings.excerpt: The rent shall be updated every year by 100% of the change in the consumer price index.
findings.explanation: For this type of lease, indexation above 75% of the ISTAT index may not be allowed. Verify it and negotiate the percentage down.

findings.title: Break option for the landlord only
findings.excerpt: The Landlord may withdraw from this Agreement at any time by giving six months' written notice. No corresponding right is granted to the Tenant.
findings.explanation: Once the tenant has fitted out the premises, a one-sided break option leaves it exposed to losing the investment on short notice. Ask for a reciprocal option, or for the reimbursement of the fit-out costs not yet amortised.

findings.title: Non-compete without compensation
findings.excerpt: For 36 months after termination, the Employee shall not work for any competitor in the European Union.
findings.explanation: A post-employment non-compete must be limited in time, place and activity, and it must be paid. Without compensation it is likely void, and three years across the whole EU is very broad.

findings.title: Overtime included in the salary with no limit
findings.excerpt: The salary covers any overtime work requested by the Company.
findings.explanation: An all-inclusive clause without a cap on hours can be challenged. State how many overtime hours the salary covers.

findings.title: The provider can change the terms unilaterally
findings.excerpt: The Provider may amend these Terms at any time by giving 7 days' notice by email.
findings.explanation: The client cannot plan on terms that can change with a week's notice. Require consent for material changes, or a right to terminate with a refund.

findings.title: No data processing agreement
findings.explanation: The provider will process personal data of the client's customers, but there are no data processing terms under article 28 of the GDPR. They should be signed before going live.

findings.title: Automatic renewal for 36 months
findings.excerpt: The subscription renews automatically for successive periods of 36 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice.
findings.explanation: A long renewal term with a long notice period locks the client in. Ask for 12-month renewals and a 30-day notice.

findings.title: Service levels without service credits
findings.excerpt: The Provider will use reasonable efforts to achieve 99.5% availability.
findings.explanation: A target without service credits or a termination right cannot be enforced in practice.

findings.title: Force majeure includes staff shortages
findings.excerpt: Force majeure includes, without limitation, strikes, lack of personnel and shortage of raw materials.
findings.explanation: Staff and material shortages are business risks the supplier controls. Listing them as force majeure lets the supplier suspend deliveries without liability.

findings.title: Prices revised at the supplier's discretion
findings.excerpt: Prices may be revised by the Supplier from time to time.
findings.explanation: Without a formula or a cap, the price is effectively open. Tie revisions to an index and give the buyer a right to terminate.

findings.title: Delivery terms not defined
findings.excerpt: Goods shall be delivered to the Buyer's premises.
findings.explanation: It is unclear who bears the risk during transport. Refer to an Incoterms rule, for example DAP.

findings.title: Immediate termination if a target is missed
findings.excerpt: If the Distributor fails to reach the minimum purchase target in any quarter, the Supplier may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect.
findings.explanation: One bad quarter can end the relationship with no time to fix it. Ask for a yearly target and a cure period before termination.

findings.title: No indemnity when the agreement ends
findings.excerpt: No indemnity of any kind shall be due to the Distributor upon termination.
findings.explanation: The distributor builds the customer base and gets nothing when the agreement ends. Consider a goodwill indemnity or a buy-back of the remaining stock.

findings.title: The German version prevails
findings.excerpt: In case of discrepancies, the German version shall prevail.
findings.explanation: If the client negotiates in English or Italian, the prevailing version should be one it can read.

findings.title: Cross-default on any group debt
findings.excerpt: An Event of Default occurs if any company of the Borrower's group fails to pay any financial debt when due.
findings.explanation: A late payment by any group company, for any amount, makes the whole loan due. Limit it to material debts above a threshold.

findings.title: Default interest may exceed the legal limit
findings.excerpt: Late payments shall bear interest at 18% per year.
findings.explanation: In Italy, interest above the usury threshold can be void. Check the rate against the current threshold for this type of loan.

findings.title: Acceleration at the lender's discretion
findings.excerpt: The Lender may declare the loan immediately due if, in its opinion, the Borrower's financial condition deteriorates.
findings.explanation: A subjective trigger gives the lender a unilateral exit. Replace it with objective financial covenants.

findings.title: Drag-along with no minimum price
findings.excerpt: Shareholders holding 60% of the shares may require all other shareholders to sell their shares to a third-party buyer.
findings.explanation: Minority shareholders can be forced to sell at any price. Add a floor, for example the fair market value set by an independent expert.

findings.title: Term longer than the legal maximum
findings.excerpt: This Agreement shall remain in force for 10 years.
findings.explanation: Under Italian law, shareholders' agreements of this kind last at most 5 years, and a longer term is reduced to 5. State the renewal rules instead.

findings.title: No deadlock mechanism
findings.explanation: With two shareholders at 50%, a disagreement can block the company. Add an escalation step and a buy-sell mechanism.

findings.title: Audit with 24 hours' notice
findings.excerpt: The Licensor may audit the Licensee's use of the Software upon 24 hours' notice.
findings.explanation: One day is too short to prepare and can disrupt operations. Ask for at least 30 days' notice, at most once a year, during business hours.

findings.title: Licenses tied to named users
findings.excerpt: Each license is assigned to a named user and cannot be transferred.
findings.explanation: When people leave the firm, their licenses are lost. Ask for the right to reassign them.

title: Settlement agreement — Theta S.r.l. and Iota S.p.A.

findings.title: The release also covers future claims
findings.excerpt: Each party releases the other from any claim, known or unknown, past or future, arising from any relationship between them.
findings.explanation: The release goes beyond the dispute being settled and may waive claims under other contracts. Limit it to the claims described in the recitals.

findings.title: Confidentiality with no consequence for a breach
findings.excerpt: The parties shall keep the terms of this settlement confidential.
findings.explanation: Without a penalty, a breach is hard to act on. Consider a fixed penalty clause.

findings.title: The franchisor may terminate without cause
findings.excerpt: The Franchisor may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving 30 days' written notice.
findings.explanation: The franchisee invests in the premises and the brand, and can lose everything with a month's notice. Limit termination to specific breaches, or add a compensation.

findings.title: Exclusive territory can be reduced at will
findings.excerpt: The Franchisor may at any time amend the Territory, including by opening or authorising other outlets within it.
findings.explanation: An exclusive territory that the franchisor can shrink is no exclusivity at all. Ask for a fixed territory for the whole term, or at least a right of first refusal on any new outlet within it.

findings.title: The entry fee is never refunded
findings.excerpt: The entry fee is not refundable under any circumstances.
findings.explanation: The fee is kept even if the franchisor never delivers the territory or the training. Make it refundable when the franchisor does not perform.

findings.title: Liquidated damages of 24 months of royalties for any breach
findings.excerpt: In case of any breach, the Franchisee shall pay liquidated damages equal to 24 months of royalties, without prejudice to further damages.
findings.explanation: A fixed penalty for any breach, even a minor one, on top of further damages, is disproportionate and a court may reduce it. Limit it to material breaches and negotiate the amount down.

findings.title: Unlimited personal guarantee by the franchisee's owner
findings.excerpt: The shareholder of the Franchisee personally and unconditionally guarantees all obligations under this Agreement, without limit of amount or time.
findings.explanation: An unlimited and perpetual personal guarantee exposes the owner's private assets beyond the life of the business. Cap it to a fixed amount and to the term of the agreement.

findings.title: Mandatory suppliers at prices set by the franchisor
findings.excerpt: The Franchisee shall buy all products exclusively from suppliers appointed by the Franchisor, at the prices communicated by the Franchisor.
findings.explanation: The franchisee's margins depend entirely on prices it cannot negotiate. Ask for a price mechanism tied to the market, or a right to use equivalent suppliers.

findings.title: Resale prices fixed by the franchisor
findings.excerpt: The Franchisee shall apply the retail prices set out in the Franchisor's price list.
findings.explanation: Imposing fixed or minimum resale prices is a hardcore restriction under EU competition rules: the clause is likely void and exposes both parties. Make the price list a recommendation.

findings.title: Royalty on gross receipts, including VAT and refunds
findings.excerpt: The Franchisee shall pay a royalty of 6% of gross receipts, before any discount, refund or tax.
findings.explanation: A royalty computed before VAT, refunds and promotional discounts inflates the base. Define turnover net of VAT, refunded sales and discounts.

findings.title: Five-year non-compete after the end
findings.excerpt: For five years after termination, the Franchisee shall not operate any coffee shop in Italy.
findings.explanation: Five years across the whole country is likely excessive. Limit it to one year and to the area of the franchised shop.

findings.title: Renewal at the franchisor's discretion, against a new entry fee
findings.excerpt: Renewal is subject to the Franchisor's approval and to the payment of a renewal fee equal to the entry fee then in force.
findings.explanation: The franchisee has no right to renew and pays the full entry fee again. Ask for a right to renew on the same terms when not in breach, and for a reduced fee.

findings.title: Unilateral changes to the operations manual
findings.excerpt: The Franchisor may amend the Operations Manual at any time, and amendments bind the Franchisee upon notice.
findings.explanation: The manual sets costs: fit-out, menu, equipment. Unlimited amendments mean unlimited mandatory investments. Require a notice period and a yearly cap on the investments the manual can impose.

findings.title: Minimum purchase obligation with no sales guarantee
findings.excerpt: The Franchisee shall purchase a minimum of EUR 120,000 of products per year, regardless of actual sales.
findings.explanation: A fixed minimum unrelated to sales shifts the whole demand risk to the franchisee. Tie the minimum to a percentage of actual turnover, or add a step-up in the first years.

findings.title: Buy-back of the equipment at book value
findings.excerpt: Upon termination, the Franchisor may take over the lease of the premises and buy the equipment at its net book value.
findings.explanation: Book value is usually far below what the franchisee paid for fit-out and equipment. Ask for fair market value, or for the right to sell to a third party.

findings.title: Marketing fund without reporting
findings.excerpt: The Franchisee shall contribute 2% of its turnover to the marketing fund managed by the Franchisor.
findings.explanation: There is no obligation to report how the fund is spent. Ask for a yearly statement.

findings.title: The franchisor owns the customer data
findings.excerpt: All customer data collected in the Outlet are the exclusive property of the Franchisor.
findings.explanation: After termination the franchisee loses its own customer base, and the clause ignores joint controllership under data protection law. Ask for shared use of the data and a data processing agreement.

findings.title: Assignment forbidden for the franchisee, free for the franchisor
findings.excerpt: The Franchisee may not assign this Agreement. The Franchisor may assign it to any third party without the Franchisee's consent.
findings.explanation: The franchisee cannot sell its business, while the franchisor can hand the relationship to anyone, even a competitor. Ask for assignment with consent not to be unreasonably withheld, on both sides.

findings.title: Disputes before a foreign court
findings.excerpt: Any dispute shall be settled exclusively by the courts of Luxembourg.
findings.explanation: Litigating abroad raises costs for an Italian franchisee. Prefer an Italian court or arbitration seated in Italy.

findings.title: Mandatory training invoiced separately
findings.excerpt: Initial and ongoing training is mandatory and will be invoiced at the Franchisor's then-current rates.
findings.explanation: The entry fee usually covers initial training; open-ended mandatory training at undetermined rates is a hidden cost. Include initial training in the fee and cap the yearly cost of ongoing training.
